newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US T-bond futures could list even lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US T-bond futures could list even lower.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures may have confirmed that an interim top is in place and could list even lower in the very near term, analysts said.
September T-bond futures hit a high for this move at 112-24/32 on June 20 and since have failed to retest that level, instead edging downward and probing increasingly lower support levels.

Analysts also argued that futures fundamentally have sucked in as much price-supportive news as they can hold, largely predicated on sentiment the Federal Reserve is unlikely to hike rates at this week's committee meeting.
"My outlook is...looking increasingly like we've put in a pretty good top," said Gerry DeMers, technical analyst at Fuji Securities Inc. "They've kind of priced in the good news."
The inflation-leery debt market also sees some key gauges such as crude oil as being close to lows of this move and thus more likely to turn higher than keep heading down, he added.

Late last Wednesday, September T-bonds broke below the neckline at roughly 111-22/32 of a head-and-shoulders pattern that had been forming since mid-June, said Holly Liss, a technical analyst at Sakura Dellsher Inc.
She said the contract tested but failed to close back above that neckline last Friday, making a fall the next couple days toward 110-17/32 to 110-10/32 more likely.
"It wouldn't surprise me if we get a full-point selloff," she said, including Monday's early 24/32 loss.
DeMers said a combination of technicals supported ideas that that T-bonds may have topped out near-term but without a long-term trend change.
He said Elliott Wave proponents viewed the rise to 112-24/32 as just an A-B-C correction, although many would bail out if bonds broke below 110-05/23.
He also said weekly stochastics were overbought in the 90s last week and could cross over again soon.
"If we end (this) week here, it would be a crossover down," he said. "It would be a confirmed sell."
Although the long-term uptrend is intact if September T-bonds keep closing above 110-02/32, Liss said the contract must close above 112-13/32 to trigger much more upside.
Failing that, she said it might wander between supports clustered near 110-02/32 or 109-25/32 and the 112-05/32 area.
DeMers said upside and downside failures could presage broad range-trade in the next few months between 105 and 112.
